issue_context.title: Socket.EndReceiveMessageFrom not Returning SocketFlags in NET6
issue_context.body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/SocketEndReceiveMessageFrom-not-Return-/10053458)._

---
When migrating from NET Framework 4.8 to NET6 we have found that on the call Socket.EndReceiveMessageFrom we no longer receive the SocketFlags.

I have attached a solution with four console applications.

SenderNET48 - This will broadcast on port 7560 using UDP, sending the current date and time as a string every 5 seconds  
SenderNET6 - same as SenderNET48 but in NET 6

ListenerNET48 - This will listen on port 7560 and output the message received and the SocketFlags returned (which will be “Broadcast” in this instance).  
ListenerNET6 - Same as ListenerNET48 but in NET6 this incorrectly returns no SocketFlags.

You can launch either SenderNET48 or SenderNET6 to start send the broadcast messages, both work the same.

then launch ListenerNET48 and ListenerNET6 both have the same code, but you will see the the NET6 version does not get the SocketFlags.

I have attached a Zip with the Entire solution for you to investigate this change in behaviour.

![image.png](https://aka.ms/dc/image?name=Bd219ea49429341aca852285bccf96661637890893446757050_20220525-162901-image.png&tid=d219ea49429341aca852285bccf96661637890893446757050)

I can confirm the repro. Looks like a .NET 6.0 regression caused by the #47229 refactor.

We have the same bug in the Task-based `ReceiveMessageFromAsync`, `SocketReceiveMessageFromResult.SocketFlags` does not contain the expected flags.

Triage: Confirmed regression, might affect people migrating to .NET from .NET Framework. We should try to fix it in 7.0.
It is on rarely used API, so if it is complicated, might be punted to Future.

review_comments: Is Linux/macOS not expected to propagate socket flags?

It should, and based on a quick look at the code, it does.

This test however works with `SocketFlags.Broadcast` (`MSG_BCAST`) which is Windows-specific. I wasn't able to construct a cross platform test that works with other flags. For that I would need for example enforce the truncation of a UDP packet (`MSG_TRUNC`). Maybe @tmds has an idea, but this is not worth wasting too much time on IMO.
maybe you can  add Linux specific test as complement....?

> I wasn't able to construct a cross platform test that works with other flags. For that I would need for example enforce the truncation of a UDP packet (MSG_TRUNC). Maybe @tmds has an idea, but this is not worth wasting too much time on IMO

To get `MSG_TRUNC` you can make the receive buffer smaller than the message that was sent.

> To get `MSG_TRUNC` you can make the receive buffer smaller than the message that was sent.

If you mean passing smaller buffer to `recvmsg` than the original packet payload sent, yeah I tried, but that did not result in `MSG_TRUNC` on Ubuntu (I guess it means that the rest of the packet is in the OS buffer so there was no truncation actually). Also tried reducing `SO_RECVBUF` but it had no effect (Maybe it does not affect OS buffers in case of UDP?)

> maybe you can add Linux specific test as complement....?

Cross-platform & Linux-specific would be both great, but I wasn't able to come up with anything.

Ubuntu 20.04.
```
furt@ubu20:/tmp/socket$ ~/dotnet-latest/dotnet run
Truncated
```

If anything I would. expect troubles on old distress or more likely platform difference on macOS or Windows.
@antonfirsov you should be able to get `MSG_TRUNC` as described above.

That works indeed on Linux, no idea what did I mess up in my previous attempt. Doesn't work on Windows though, we are getting a `WSAEMSGSIZE` error with async, and no indication of the truncation with sync API-s.

I ended up pushing a complementary test `ReceiveTruncated_TruncatedFlagIsSetOnReceive`. Limited to `AnyUnix` for now, let's see how it goes on the CI.
